QF.id: AIF Valuation Taxation and Good Practices_35

question.text: Impermissible avoidance under GAAR includes arrangements where:

answer.text: Main purpose is tax benefit, rights not at arm's length, or arrangement lacks commercial substance

explanation.text: The Logic: Per NISM XIX-A (p. 264), an arrangement can be declared an impermissible avoidance arrangement under GAAR when its main purpose is to obtain a tax benefit AND at least one of the specified tests is met: rights/obligations not at arm's length, lack or deemed lack of commercial substance, misuse or abuse of the Income-tax Act, or being carried out in a non-bona-fide manner. The Trap: Genuine tax planning, legitimate investor returns, or SEBI registration of the AIF do not by themselves invoke GAAR. The trigger is the combination of tax-benefit purpose with one of the listed tests. Note: Distributors should flag transaction structures that appear to lack commercial substance, as these may invite GAAR scrutiny.
